WebAPI: make the plugin build explicit via WITH_WEBAPI

The WebAPI plugin's CMake silently emits a WARNING and omits the
plugin from the build whenever no Qt HTTP server module is found. A
packager who forgets the Qt HttpServer dependency therefore gets a
quietly incomplete package, and the missing plugin is only noticed
much later by end users.

Add a WITH_WEBAPI option (default ON, consistent with the other
WITH_* options) and turn the silent omission into a FATAL_ERROR: when
the plugin is requested but no Qt HTTP server is available, the
configure step now fails with an actionable message. Skipping the
plugin requires an explicit -DWITH_WEBAPI=OFF.

LDAP: mention FreeIPA in the distinguished-name group member option

FreeIPA (389 Directory Server) stores group membership in the "member"
attribute as distinguished names, exactly like Samba/AD - not as login
names like a plain OpenLDAP setup.

The "Group member identification" radio button is labelled
"Distinguished name (Samba/AD)", so FreeIPA administrators tend to pick
the other option ("... user login name ... (OpenLDAP)") instead. With
that scheme the "groups of user" query builds the filter
"member=<login>", which never matches the DN values stored by FreeIPA,
and group-based access control silently stops working.

Add FreeIPA to the label so the correct scheme is obvious.

(cherry picked from commit f6ae0aa1d332afd33a27db9c5ea7f90d1f6f7cd2)

Configurator: hide x11vnc parameters label in standard view

On the Service tab of the configurator, selecting the builtin x11vnc
server showed the "Custom x11vnc parameters:" label with no input field
next to it in standard view mode. Both x11vnc properties (the X Damage
checkbox and the extra arguments line edit) carry the Advanced flag, so
the input widgets were hidden, but the static QLabel from the .ui file
has no associated property and stayed visible.

Mark the whole X11VncConfigurationWidget as advanced, the same way
DemoConfigurationPage marks its page, so the label is hidden together
with the input fields in standard view and shown again in advanced view.

(cherry picked from commit be50a54c111d4aab197466358db4325d66cede38)

Configurator: auto-increment default names for new objects

When creating multiple locations, computers, applications or websites in
the configurator, every new item received the identical default name
("New location", "New computer", ...), producing indistinguishable
duplicate entries that are easy to confuse.

Add ObjectManager::generateUniqueName(), which returns the base name when
it is still free and otherwise appends an incrementing numeric suffix
("New location 2", "New location 3", ...). Use it in the builtin
directory and desktop services configuration pages when adding objects.

Add Wayland input blocking via setuid EVIOCGRAB daemon

Add a privileged daemon (veyon-input-helper) that runs as root via setuid
and listens on a Unix socket for block/unblock commands. The daemon uses
EVIOCGRAB on /dev/input/event* to block physical input devices on Wayland
where the Veyon Server runs as a regular user.

Components:
- input-block-helper.c: setuid root daemon, Unix socket at
  /run/veyon/input-block.sock, select() event loop, sigsuspend for
  signal-safe wait, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG for orphan cleanup, auto-creates
  /run/veyon directory and socket with world-readable permissions
- InputBlockHelper: Qt wrapper using QLocalSocket to communicate with
  the daemon, spawns/terminates the daemon process, retry-after-spawn
  for socket readiness, killall fallback for cleaning up stale daemons
- LinuxInputDeviceFunctions: delegates Wayland blocking to
  InputBlockHelper; enableInputDevices() always runs unblock on Wayland
  to handle startup cleanup

  server on StartLock (in addition to forwarding to the worker for the
  visual LockWidget); StopLock always calls enableInputDevices()
  regardless of worker state; cleanup runs on both Service and Server
  component startup

DemoServer: rework FBU queue to sequence/epoch sync and safe reconnect

Refactor demo framebuffer update forwarding to keep all clients on a single
ordered message stream and avoid per-client state divergence.

Key changes:
- Replace keyframe/index-based replay with global FBU sequence tracking.
- Store queued FBUs with timestamps and let each client track its own sequence
  position.
- Discard only messages that are no longer needed by any connected client.
- Add epoch-based stream reset semantics across reconnects.
- Reconnect to the local VNC server and reset protocol state when lag exceeds
  queue age limits, then restart from a clean stream.
- Track active DemoServerConnection instances and clean them up on reconnect.
- Copy pending messages under read lock, then write to sockets outside the lock.
- Add VncClientProtocol::reset() for explicit protocol state reinitialization.
- Adjust demo default framebuffer update interval (100 ms -> 50 ms).
- Remove lastUpdatedRect/keyframe coupling that no longer applies with
  sequence-based queueing.

This fixes issues with zlib-encoded rectangles since especially with the
Tight encoding the zlib streams can get out of sync if any updates are
missing / a demo client joins too late.

VncClientProtocol: drop lastUpdatedRect()

As of the recent rewrite, DemoServer no longer relies on detecting full
framebuffer updates.
